title: Minimum wage 2026: government projects R$ 1,741 for 2027
subtitle: Minister of Finance presents estimate that will be included in the budget sent to Congress
excerpt: The federal government estimates the minimum wage will reach R$ 1,741 in 2027, a value that should appear in the budget bill sent to Congress.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The announcement of the new estimate for the minimum wage in 2027 has mobilized workers, employers, and analysts, as it sets the remuneration baseline for the next fiscal year. The R$ 1,741 projection emerges in the context of a budget that forecasts a surplus and maintains the indexation of social benefits to the wage floor.

Official estimate for 2027

Minister of Finance Dario Durigan informed that the federal government estimates the minimum wage will be R$ 1,741 in 2027. The figure is expected to appear in the Annual Budget Law Bill (PLOA) to be forwarded to the National Congress by the 31st of this month.

Floor definition process

According to the 2027 Budget Guidelines Bill (PLDO), the initial proposal calculated the minimum wage at R$ 1,717. The value may still change until December 2026, when the November National Consumer Price Index (INPC), the legal basis for the final adjustment, is released.

Maintenance of benefit indexation

Durigan ruled out the de-indexation of the minimum wage in social benefits, stating that the adjustments provided by law will also be applied to Social Security and other assistance programs that follow floor indexation.

Dieese calculation for a family of four

The Inter-Union Department of Statistics and Socioeconomic Studies (Dieese) estimates that the minimum wage necessary to support a family of four would be R$ 7,425.99, equivalent to 4.58 times the current value of R$ 1,621.

Next steps and calendar

The definitive minimum wage will be known in December 2026, following the publication of the November INPC. Meanwhile, the budget proposal that includes the R$ 1,741 estimate continues its legislative process in Congress, where it will be analyzed and voted on by lawmakers.

With information from G1.
